messages:
jon (support): Heads up — found what looks like a Redwood API key inside a customer-provided release archive attached to ticket #4532. file: /attachments/4532/release_v2.tar.gz. I pulled a small redacted snippet: `RK-1a2b3c4d...` — tagging sec for triage
alert-bot: automated-secrets-scan detected pattern MATCH in /attachments/4532/release_v2.tar.gz (rule: redwood-api-key-v1). Ticket 4532 created by @jon.
maria (sec): Thanks @jon. Do we know which key ID this maps to (full id from inventory) and the owner service/account? Also, any evidence of external use yet?
jon (support): Not yet, I only opened the ticket and attached the archive. I can upload the full filename to a secure share if you want to fetch it. The snippet above is all I redacted for the thread.
maria (sec): Please don't distribute the full key in Slack. Kevin — can you run a quick inventory lookup and last-used query for the prefix `RK-1a2b`? If it's a valid live key we should revoke immediately and rotate.
kevin (infra): Running `keydb lookup --prefix RK-1a2b` now. Also checking auth logs for last 90 days.
kevin (infra): lookup result: key id RK-1a2b3c4d5e belongs to service-account `svc-support-onboarding` (created 2021-09-03). Scopes: read:models, embeddings:create. Policy: non-admin.
kevin (infra): auth log peek: one successful call 2026-03-15T03:12:08Z from ip 137.45.9.3 to /v1/embeddings (usage ~120 tokens). Several failed auth attempts 2026-02-21 from 54.23.10.8 (rate-limited). No large-scale token usage.
sam (product-safety): If this belongs to a support onboarding service account, likely low blast radius, but it was included in a customer archive — possible customer accidentally packaged it. Need to confirm whether the archive was uploaded to a public repo or shared externally.
maria (sec): Agreed. Immediate actions: (1) Kevin — revoke RK-1a2b3c4d5e now and issue replacement with minimal scopes; (2) Jon — pull the customer archive into secure sandbox and check if there are any other secrets included (don't extract on local laptop); (3) Kevin/Maria — run a full audit for any other keys owned by svc-support-onboarding and check for similar exposures; (4) Sam — prepare a short comms draft in case customers need notification.
kevin (infra): Revoking now with internal runbook command: `keyctl revoke RK-1a2b3c4d5e --reason leaked-in-archive --by kevin` -> success. New key created `RK-rot-9f8e7d6c` with same scopes but will rotate to more restrictive after we confirm callers.
jon (support): Downloading archive to secure S3 sandbox at s3://sec-sandbox/4532/release_v2.tar.gz. Scanning with `secretscan` and `trufflehog` now.
jon (support): Scan notes: found the same key in file `scripts/setup_env.sh` and an internal helper config `support/.redwoodrc`. No other Redwood secrets detected. There are several customer tokens for third-party services as well.
maria (sec): Good containment step. Kevin — check if the IP that used the key (137.45.9.3) maps to an internal CI runner or an external host. If external, pull network flow logs and S3 access logs for the ticket attachment.
kevin (infra): 137.45.9.3 resolves to a cloud provider IP (digitalocean maybe) and was a single successful call from 2026-03-15. No other activity. S3 access logs show ticket creator (internal user) uploaded the archive on 2026-03-10 and then support engineer downloaded it on 2026-03-11. No public exposure detected (object ACL private).
maria (sec): Preliminary conclusion: customer archive accidentally included our support service account key; it was packaged during a support interaction but never published publicly. Blast radius appears limited. Still treating as leak.
sam (product-safety): For customer comms — since the object was private and there is no sign of exfiltration, recommend an internal-only incident note and an offer to rotate customer-side secrets if they want. No public customer breach notice. I'll draft language and share.
maria (sec): Post-incident actions: 1) Rotate any remaining keys owned by `svc-support-onboarding` and rotate to short-lived tokens where possible (owner: kevin, due EOD). 2) Update support runbooks to scrub internal keys from artifacts before returning archives to customers (owner: jon & support docs, due 72h). 3) Add a pre-upload scanner in support UI to warn when files contain internal tokens (owner: infra + devex, due 2 weeks). 4) Add inventory tag enforcement to prevent long-lived service keys without automatic rotation (owner: sec+infra, due 30 days).
maria (sec): Creating incident record: INC-2026-048. Please add any logs or artifact links to the ticket.
jon (support): Added sandbox object link and scan output to INC-2026-048. Also started a short checklist for support to avoid exporting full env files.
kevin (infra): Confirmed rotation completed for all keys tied to svc-support-onboarding. No remaining active long-lived keys for that service.
maria (sec): Great. Closing immediate ticket here. We'll follow up with the action items above and a short retrospective next week. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
sam (product-safety): +1 — will share comms draft in INC-2026-048.
jon (support): Thanks team.
